samples.text:
The diagram shows the process of recycling plastic bottles to make polyester fibre for clothes. There are eight stages in the process.

First, the bottles are collected from homes. Then they are sorted, and the PET bottles are separated from another plastics. After that, the bottles are washed and the labels and caps is removed. At the end of this stage the bottles are clean.

Next, the bottles are shredded, it means they are cut into small flakes. So the bottles become small pieces of plastic. Then the flakes are melted at 260°C and become liquid. After this, the liquid is pushed through a very tiny holes and it forms threads. This is the extrusion stage.

In the seventh stage, the threads are stretched and they are spun into yarn. Finally, the fabric is made and it is sewed into jackets and T-shirts.

Overall, the process begin with old plastic bottles and ends with new clothes. Most of the stages are about changing the bottles into thread, and only the last stage is about making the clothes.
samples.why: Basic overview at the end · all eight stages covered in order with the key figure · mechanical linking · adequate vocabulary · several agreement, article and word form errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The diagram illustrates how used plastic bottles are recycled and turned into polyester fibre, which is then used to make clothing.

Overall, the process consists of eight stages, starting with the collection of bottles from homes and ending with the production of garments such as jackets and T-shirts. The bottles are first prepared, then melted and turned into threads, and finally made into fabric, which shows how a waste product can become the raw material for new goods.

At the beginning, bottles are collected from households and sorted so that PET bottles are separated from other types of plastic. They are then washed, and their labels and caps are removed. Following this, the bottles are shredded into small flakes, which are melted at a temperature of 260°C so that they become liquid.

The liquid plastic is next pushed through tiny holes in the extrusion stage, forming threads. These threads is stretched and spun into yarn, which is the material used for making fabric. In the final stage, fabric is woven from the yarn and sewn into items of clothing, in particular jackets and T-shirts.
samples.why: Clear overview grouping the stages into three phases · logical progression with passives and sequencers · appropriate vocabulary (shredded, extrusion, garments) · mostly error-free with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
The diagram explains how discarded plastic bottles, collected from ordinary households, are reprocessed into polyester fibre and ultimately into clothing.

The process involves eight sequential stages and can be seen as a transformation from solid waste to wearable fabric: the bottles are first prepared and broken down, then melted and reformed into threads, and finally woven and sewn into garments. Notably, the only temperature specified is that of the melting stage, the point at which the bottles lose their original form.

Initially, bottles are collected from households and taken to be sorted, with PET bottles being separated from other plastics, a step that ensures only PET continues through the process. After being washed and stripped of their labels and caps, they are shredded into flakes. These flakes are melted at a temperature of 260°C, and the resulting liquid is extruded, meaning that it is forced through tiny holes to create fine threads.

In the penultimate stage, the threads are stretched and spun into yarn. This yarn is then woven into fabric, which is sewn to produce clothing such as jackets and T-shirts, bringing the process to a close.
samples.why: Insightful overview tracing the change from waste to fabric · stages sequenced precisely · wide, accurate vocabulary (reprocessed, extruded, penultimate) · varied complex structures · error-free.
